clue.text: Like one who cares

parts.note: a description of someone thoughtful who minds the feelings of others

explanation.definitionFit: Being thoughtful of others' feelings is the mark of a caring person.

clue.text: But square cuts are made in this ground

definitions.text: But square cuts are made in this ground

parts.words: But square cuts are made in this ground
parts.note: a square cut is a cricket stroke, played at a famous London cricket ground whose name is a rounded shape, the opposite of square

explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground; a square cut is a cricket shot, and 'square' plays against the ground's rounded name.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Test cricket ground in Kennington is named for its elliptical shape.

clue.text: Slough outbuilding

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off, as a snake does its skin
a hut in the garden

explanation.definitionFit: A snake casts off its skin, and a garden hut for tools is also this word.

clue.text: Light DIY team turning out

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters are turned around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A do-it-yourself crew arriving to work in daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges the letters of DIY TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of daylight are the time when it is light.

clue.text: Stroked, we hear, in a way

indicators.note: says the word is identified by how it is spoken out loud

parts.note: a stroke rows the boat, so stroked means rowed

explanation.surface: Someone petted, so people say, in a particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns ROWED into its soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A route or street is a way to travel along.

clue.text: Old contact takes time over lawsuit

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting over another comes before it

parts.note: an action is a case brought in court

explanation.surface: A former acquaintance takes years to settle a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts T above ACTION in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic word for touching or physical contact.

clue.text: Ironmonger and computer dealer

definitions.meaning: a seller of tools and household metal goods
one selling computer equipment, the machine side of computing

explanation.definitionFit: A tool and pots seller in an ironmonger's shop, and someone selling physical computing kit rather than programs.

clue.text: Change of gear depends on it

definitions.text: Change of gear depends on it

parts.words: Change of gear depends on it
parts.note: gear means clothing, and a change of clothes is hung out to dry on it

explanation.definitionFit: Washing, a change of clothes, is pegged to and hangs from a garden line.

clue.text: Beetle in royal drive

definitions.meaning: a beetle is a heavy wooden mallet
the London avenue running to Buckingham Palace

explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is a heavy wooden hammer, for which this is an old word, and London's ceremonial road to Buckingham Palace bears the name.

clue.text: Marriage for security cannot be struck just anywhere

definitions.meaning: a match is a marriage, here one made to be safe
this kind of match lights only on the special strip on its box

explanation.surface: A marriage made for safety, unlike a casual fling, cannot be entered just anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a match ignites only against the prepared side of its box, and a marriage is also a match.

clue.text: Lump of lead I trace in entrance to mine

indicators.note: a lump is a chunk taken out of something, so a run of letters is lifted from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A miner finds a chunk of lead ore at the pit entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lump of' signals letters lifted out of 'lead I trace', across the word joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage driven into a hillside as access to a mine.

clue.text: Wickets near collapsing batsman is so afraid

indicators.note: a collapsing structure falls apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: With stumps about to fall, the batsman is terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges the letters of WICKETS NEAR; the batsman is a cricketer facing the bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with awe or dread, overwhelmed by fear.

clue.text: Knitting wools — and per ounce?

indicators.note: knitting works strands together in a new pattern, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A knitting pattern listing wool, and its price per ounce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knitting' rearranges WOOLS AND PER; an ounce is not a weight but a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the big pale spotted cat of the Himalaya.

clue.text: Attractive to lose a few also, presumably

definitions.meaning: charming, engaging

definitions.text: to lose a few also, presumably
definitions.meaning: from the saying that you ... and lose some

explanation.surface: Someone charming in defeat, taking the occasional loss in good spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half leans on the saying 'you win some, you lose some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and engaging, as a sweet smile is; and the stock saying pairs winning a few with losing a few.

clue.text: New York island infernal on the inside?

indicators.note: only the inner part of the word counts, so its first and last letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A New York island that is a hell when seen from within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the inside' keeps the middle of HELLISH, losing its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The immigration station island in New York Harbor, where arrivals were processed.

clue.text: Cost of tying up boat makes one low with anger

parts.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes

explanation.surface: Paying harbour fees leaves a sailor depressed and furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like 'depressed' but is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring charges are the fee paid for berthing a vessel.

clue.text: Schoolboy producing inferior degree

definitions.meaning: at English public schools the younger of two brothers is called this
of lesser rank or importance

explanation.definitionFit: Someone under age, or a younger brother at school; and lesser in importance.

clue.text: Early importer of marbles?

parts.note: the earl who brought sculptures from the Parthenon in Athens to Britain, not a toy-marble dealer

explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin shipped the Parthenon sculptures to Britain in the early nineteenth century; they are named after him.

clue.text: Cut up, North was, in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the letters of these words are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A Northerner was out of sorts and withdrawn after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns N plus WAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber that has been cut into pieces with a saw is described this way.

clue.text: Timber contract

definitions.meaning: pine or fir wood in planks
an agreement or bargain

explanation.definitionFit: Pine or fir planking goes by this name, and a bargain struck between parties is also one.

clue.text: One is turfed out of course

definitions.text: One is turfed out of course

parts.words: One is turfed out of course
parts.note: a chunk of turf hacked out by a golf club on a golf course, not someone expelled naturally

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's shot often gouges a piece of turf out of the fairway.

clue.text: Get doctor as nervous twitch follows — it is serious

indicators.note: the twitch comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary spasm

explanation.surface: Get medical help as a nervous tic sets in, since it is grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' places TIC after DR and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme or severe measures are radical and grave.

clue.text: A fluter's pieces make us ready to cry

indicators.note: something in pieces is broken up, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A flute player's music moves the listeners to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' rearranges A FLUTER; the 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: On the verge of weeping, with eyes welling up.

clue.text: Joints of midshipmen?.

definitions.meaning: cannabis cigarettes
naval slang for junior officers who handled the reefing of sails

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cannabis cigarettes, and old naval slang for midshipmen, who reefed the sails.

clue.text: … to forbear is such a burden at sea

definitions.meaning: to hold back from doing something
the burden of a song is its recurring chorus

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a sailor's load at sea is something to avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'burden' is an old word for a song's chorus, the part sung repeatedly in a sea shanty.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back from acting, and the repeated chorus of a song, as sung in a shanty.

clue.text: Reproduction is some matter for printers

definitions.meaning: a duplicate or replica
text supplied to be typeset

explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate of an original, and the text a newspaper sends to be typeset.

clue.text: Percentage of a Government head at No. To?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the setter wrote No. 10, the Prime Minister's address, and the figures 1 and 0 are read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: What share does the Prime Minister at Number 10 take?
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes G from Government. The page shows 'To' where the setter's '10' (Downing Street) stood; its figures read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium or charge paid on exchanging currency, expressed as a percentage.

clue.text: See hat and nothing else on the bathing beach

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A bather wearing nothing but a hat at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A public open-air pool or swimming beach.

clue.text: It is daily taken from Windermere

definitions.meaning: a daily is a cleaning lady who comes in each day
a fish of the trout family caught in Lake Windermere

explanation.surface: Something caught daily in the English Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Windermere is a lake in England's Lake District, home of a cold-water fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning woman, also called a daily, and a trout-like fish of the Lake District lakes.

clue.text: It makes one dry up in Cambridge, for example

definitions.text: It makes one dry up in Cambridge, for example

parts.words: It makes one dry up in Cambridge, for example
parts.note: an actor who dries forgets lines through nerves; Cambridge suggests the drama of its student theatre

explanation.surface: Something that parches a person in a university town.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'dry' is theatre slang for forgetting one's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervousness before an audience makes a performer forget lines, which actors call drying.

clue.text: Piece of the crude, unbleached type of linen

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scrap of rough natural cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of' takes letters from across 'the crude'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for raw, describing the greyish-beige colour of undyed cloth.

clue.text: Train directors of former education authority

parts.note: to school is to teach or train
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Railway executives running an old local authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as a railway but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Before 1902, English elementary schools were run by locally elected bodies with this name.
